seoDescription: Learn how to create a dynamic stacking card effect on scroll using Elementor Flexbox Containers, a powerful feature for modern web design. This step-by-step tutorial guides you through building a visually engaging section without writing a single line of code. You'll master the use of nested containers, apply sticky motion effects with calculated offsets, and manage z-index properties to achieve the perfect overlapping animation. The guide also provides detailed instructions on making the entire effect fully responsive for tablet and mobile devices.

chapters.title: Initial Section and Container Setup
chapters.description: This chapter covers setting up the main 100vh section and the primary content container that will hold the stacking cards.

chapters.title: Designing the First Stacking Card
chapters.description: This chapter details how to build the first card using nested containers for text and a background image, and how to apply initial styling.

chapters.title: Duplicating Cards and Setting Z-Index
chapters.description: Learn how to duplicate the card structure and assign sequential z-index values to control the stacking order during the scroll animation.

chapters.title: Applying Sticky Motion Effects
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to apply the 'Sticky Top' motion effect to each card with progressively larger offsets to create the stacking illusion.

chapters.title: Refining the Scroll with 'Stay In Column'
chapters.description: Discover how to use the 'Stay In Column' setting to ensure the entire card section scrolls away properly after the sticky animation concludes.

chapters.title: Experimenting with Padding for Scroll Duration
chapters.description: This chapter explores how adding bottom padding to the parent container can extend the duration of the sticky scroll effect.

chapters.title: Making the Effect Responsive on Tablet
chapters.description: Learn to adapt the stacking card layout for tablet screens by changing the container direction to vertical and adjusting sizes and padding.

chapters.title: Adapting the Layout for Mobile View
chapters.description: This section covers the process of making final adjustments for mobile devices, focusing on reducing padding and setting container width for better spacing.

chapters.title: Final Mobile Tweaks and Outro
chapters.description: This final chapter shows how to fix card overlap on mobile by increasing internal padding and concludes the tutorial with a call to action.

summary:
## Core Concept: Stacking Sticky Containers
This tutorial demonstrates how to create a visually appealing effect where content cards stack on top of each other as the user scrolls down the page. The effect is achieved entirely within the Elementor editor using **Flexbox Containers** and **Motion Effects**, with no custom code required.

## Initial Structure Setup
- **Main Section:** Start with a container set to **100 VH** (Viewport Height) to create a full-screen section.
- **Wrapper Container:** Inside the main section, add a child container that will hold the stacking cards.
  - **Width:** `75%`
  - **Content Alignment:** Justify `Center` and Align `Center`.

## Designing a Reusable Card
Each "card" is a container with a specific structure that can be duplicated.
- **Card Container:**
  - **Direction:** `Row (Horizontal)`
  - **Height:** `50 VH`
  - **Styling:** Set a background color and a `25px` border-radius.
- **Content:** The card is split into two inner containers:
  - **Text Container:** Holds `Heading` and `Text Editor` widgets. This container needs internal padding for spacing (e.g., `60px` top/bottom, `95px` left/right).
  - **Image Container:** Instead of an image widget, the image is set as the container's **background**. Set a `25px` border-radius to match the parent card.

## Implementing the Stacking Effect
This is a three-step process for each card you want to stack.

### 1. Z-Index
To control which card appears on top, you must set a **Z-Index** for each card container under the `Advanced` tab.
- Assign an increasing **Z-Index** to each subsequent card:
  - Card 1: `z-index: 1`
  - Card 2: `z-index: 2`
  - Card 3: `z-index: 3`

### 2. Sticky Motion Effects
The core animation comes from the **Sticky** motion effect.
- Go to `Advanced > Motion Effects`.
- Set **Sticky:** `Top`.
- **Sticky On:** Enable for `Desktop`, `Tablet`, and `Mobile`.
- **Offset:** This value determines how far from the top of the viewport the element will "stick".

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The offset for each card must be cumulative to create space between the stacked cards. If each should have a `50px` visible gap:
> - **Card 1:** `Offset: 50`
> - **Card 2:** `Offset: 100` (`50` for Card 1's offset + `50` for its own gap)
> - **Card 3:** `Offset: 150` (`100` from Card 2's offset + `50` for its own gap)

### 3. Stay In Column
By default, sticky elements are relative to the viewport, which causes content below the section to scroll up *behind* them.
- To fix this, set **Effects Relative To:** `Stay In Column`.
- This contains the sticky effect within its parent. Once the last card has finished its animation, the entire parent container will scroll up naturally with the rest of the page.

## Responsive Adjustments
The horizontal desktop layout needs to be adjusted for smaller screens.

### Tablet View
- **Direction:** Change the card containers' direction from `Row` to `Column (Vertical)`.
- **Sizing:** Adjust the height of the image container (e.g., `30 VH`) and the font sizes.
- **Spacing:** Reduce padding and the gap between elements.

### Mobile View
- **Spacing:** Further reduce padding values (e.g., `30px` top/bottom, `40px` left/right).
- **Width:** Set the main card container's width to `95%` to create some space from the screen edges.

> [!TIP]
> If cards overlap too much on mobile, increasing the **top and bottom padding** inside each card container (e.g., to `50px`) can create more vertical space as they stack. This is often a better solution than altering the sticky offsets for different devices.
